newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand reaffirms one China policy.
newsitem.headline: Thailand reaffirms one China policy.

text.p: Thailand on Friday reassured China that it would stand firm on its one-China policy and said it looked forward to improved Chinese-U.S. relations for peace and stability in the region.
Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh gave the assurance to visiting Defence Minister Chi Haotian at a meeting.
Thailand does not recognise Taiwan, which China regards as a renegade province.
"Chi told me that he was confident that China-U.S. relations will improve and I hope that will contribute to peace and stability in the region," Chavalit told reporters after the meeting.
Chi, who is on his way home from the United States, is on an official visit and arrived here late on Thursday. He leaves on Saturday.

"I also told him that Thailand will try all its means to help support the peace and reconciliation effort in Cambodia," Chavalit said, describing the situation in Cambodia as worrying without elaboration.
The fragile Cambodian coalition government is faced with a political rift between co-prime ministers Prince Norodom Ranarridh and Hun Sen.

He said that China and Thailand, who shared a common border with Burma, agreed to continue constructive engagement with the ruling military State Law and Order Restoration Council and maintain a policy of non-intervention in Rangoon's internal affairs.
He also pledged to improve Thai military cooperation with China.
